tagline: Sixty-eight miles around the grand lake of the Ojibwe.
intro: Out of Isle the loop sets off around Mille Lacs on Highways 169, 27, 18 and 47 and a county stretch called Shakopee Lake Road, 68 paved miles through Wahkon, Onamia, Garrison and Malmo. The lake is big and shallow, no deeper than 42 feet anywhere. The Ojibwe call it Misi-zaaga'igan, the grand lake.

In winter it freezes into more than 132,500 acres of ice, and the fishing houses out on it number in the thousands. In the southwest corner sits Spirit Island, a third of an acre of pink and white granite boulders, and one of two islands in the lake set aside as a national wildlife refuge.

moments.title: Mille Lacs Kathio State Park
moments.text: Nineteen archaeological sites lie in the park, and its very name is a misreading of Izatys, which an explorer wrote down in 1679 in a hand that turned the Iz into a K.

moments.title: Mille Lacs Indian Museum and Trading Post
moments.text: In the Four Seasons Room, life-size dioramas made in 1964 follow an Ojibwe year from berry picking and wild ricing to winter trapping and the spring sugar camp.

moments.title: Garrison
moments.text: On the northwest shore the Garrison Concourse, right on Highway 169, is where the byway's listing sends early risers to watch the sun come up.
